note: Six small orthogonal state machines (revision 1 after adversarial review R1/R2: hold release re-evaluates, revocation suspends runs, no override of unscanned bytes, expectations satisfied only by accepted runs, explicit record machine) replace the 21-state single lifecycle proposed in the mission brief. Each transition is executed by one durable command (Echelon.Execution) or recorded by an authorized human decision command; history is append-only, current state is a reconstructable projection. Artifact 'Quarantined' is unrelated to Echelon.Execution's command state 'Quarantined' (poison command); UI and logs always qualify the machine name.

machines.purpose: A promise that a source will deliver something by a deadline (daily bank report, monthly BMF release, payroll file). Exists before any bytes; drives missing and late detection.

states.meaning: Awaiting delivery for an expected business date inside or before its window
Window plus grace passed without an accepted delivery; an exception case is open
A matching artifact (or artifact set) for the expected business date was released; its Run has not yet completed
An authorized pause covers the source; the window does not run
A Run for the expected business date and sequence Completed; the source's completeness watermark advanced
An authorized person declared the delivery not required, with reason; a later delivery opens an 'unexpected delivery' exception

transitions.authorization: profile expectation rule (business date and sequence must match)
Run Completed for the expected business date
Run Rejected, Cancelled or Superseded without a replacement

machines.purpose: Custody and security of one immutable byte sequence (a file, an API record batch, a scanned page set, or a member of an artifact set). Identity = generated ArtifactId; content identity = SHA-256 bound to the stored object version.

states.meaning: An intake slot exists (row committed) and bytes are being written to quarantine storage; nothing may read them
Upload interrupted or never completed within the slot lifetime; any partial object is deleted by the reconciler
Bytes complete, hashed and durable; awaiting or undergoing security inspection. Inspection attempts are a projection, not states

Security policy refused the artifact (type not permitted, structure mismatch, malware, limits, encryption or password protection, failed source authentication or integrity). Never-released bytes are kept only for the security-evidence period; PDFs with active content are not rejected but released only as derivatives (UNB-ING-SEC-010)
Inspection passed under a recorded policy version; the artifact may be parsed or presented through safe derivatives

A released artifact was found unsafe or altered (re-inspection, threat report, integrity failure); downloads are blocked, every non-submitted Run derived from it is Suspended, and an impact case lists derived records and commands

transitions.authorization: intake authorization already checked for source, tenant and profile purpose
transitions.evidence: size, SHA-256, storage checksum and version id, channel evidence

transitions.authorization: profile source authentication (signature, host key, client credential)
security policy version; clean verdict for exact hash and version
transitions.evidence: structure verdict, scanner engine and signature version, limits observed, derivative ids

transitions.authorization: re-inspection verdict, threat report or integrity failure under the security policy
ingestion.security.resolve; retention follows the highest derived class (UNB-ING-RET-001)
second managed engine's clean verdict on the exact hash and version recorded as evidence; not available for integrity failures

machines.purpose: One processing of one released artifact or complete artifact set (or one API record batch) under one profile version. Re-processing is a new run. Evidence documents do not use Runs.

states.meaning: Created for a released artifact; waiting for dependencies declared by the profile (e.g. prior day's statement)
Isolated parser converts bytes to typed staged records and computes control totals; validation runs in the same step
Every command reached a terminal state but some records have an ambiguous external outcome (reconciliation obligations open)
Every record outcome is final (none Valid, Held, Submitted, KeyConflict or OutcomeUnknown). Partial processing is Completed with non-zero rejected counts
Structural failure (schema version unknown, control totals disagree, header/trailer invalid) or an authorized decision rejected a held run; no record was submitted
Every record has an outcome (valid, invalid, duplicate, held). This is the dry-run result; nothing has been submitted

A hold rule fired (invalid share, value limit, volume, drift, dependency timeout or inspection fault); releasing it returns the Run to Validated, where hold rules, approval policy and submission mode are evaluated again in that order
Business policy (not the file itself) requires approval of the effects, e.g. migration opening balances or a manual journal batch
The source artifact was revoked while the Run had not submitted; nothing may submit until the artifact is reinstated or the Run is rejected

Valid records are being submitted as business commands through the same intake as the interface, using principal-independent business idempotency keys; guard: artifact still Released, source not paused, approval and submission-mode conditions satisfied
Every valid record has a durable command receipt; outcomes pending
A corrected artifact replaced this run before submission; after submission, corrections are reversal commands, not supersession
An authorized person cancelled before submission

transitions.authorization: profile dependency rule; source not paused
correction rule: same source, same business date, later sequence; serialised with submission on the source ordering key

transitions.evidence: record outcome counts, totals declared vs computed

transitions.authorization: infrastructure or sandbox fault (never a terminal rejection)
approval policy of the target commands (evaluated second)

submission mode automatic (institution and government sources only); guards: artifact Released at current policy version; source not paused; hold rules clear; approval satisfied or not required; submission mode satisfied

requester confirms the preview and holds authority for every target command; guards: artifact Released at current policy version; source not paused; hold rules clear; approval satisfied or not required; submission mode satisfied
correction rule, serialised with submission on the source ordering key
ingestion.run.release-hold; cannot be the uploader when the profile demands segregation; releases the hold only
ingestion.run.supersede (a held run is never superseded automatically)

approval policy of the target commands (dual control where required); guards: artifact Released at current policy version; source not paused; hold rules clear; approval satisfied or not required; submission mode satisfied
transitions.evidence: approvers bound to the content hash

transitions.authorization: artifact returned to Released (false positive confirmed); processing restarts from the beginning
Echelon.Execution receipts; intake refusals become record outcomes (KeyConflict, Declined)
transitions.evidence: command id or refusal per record

transitions.authorization: a record-level hold is released and the record submitted as its own command linked to the run
no record Valid, Held, Submitted, KeyConflict or OutcomeUnknown
every command terminal; some outcomes ambiguous

machines.purpose: Agreement between Unbound's ledger and an external observation set for one scope (bank account and business date; custodian account and as-of date; payment partner and settlement date). Matched and Resolved scopes are immutable; a later restatement, return or ledger correction for a closed scope opens a new reconciliation item in the current period linked to the closed scope (UNB-ING-FIN-007), and the closed scope shows the link.

states.meaning: Observation set and ledger period present; matching not finished
Every item matched by deterministic rules within tolerance
Unmatched or mismatched items remain; each is an exception case with ageing
Every break closed by a correcting command, a timing explanation that later matched, or an authorized write-off with evidence

transitions.authorization: reconciliation.break.resolve (write-off requires dual control and threshold)

machines.purpose: Lifecycle of stored bytes and derived personal data independent of processing state.

states.meaning: Within the retention period of the artifact's record class
A legal hold applies; disposal is impossible regardless of period
Retention period ended and no hold; disposal scheduled
Bytes and safe derivatives destroyed; a tombstone keeps id, hash, class, dates and the disposal authority. Ledger entries derived from the artifact are never disposed with it

transitions.authorization: retention schedule version; disposal batch approved by records owner

machines.purpose: Outcome of one input record of a Run. Invariant (UNB-ING-FIN-003): outcome counts equal input count; at Completed no record is Valid, Held, Submitted, KeyConflict or OutcomeUnknown.

states.meaning: Parsed and awaiting evaluation
Passed validation; eligible for submission
Failed validation; reasons and source position retained; corrections arrive as new records in a new run
Same natural key and same payload hash already accepted; reference to the original; no effect
Same natural key with a different payload hash, or an intake idempotency conflict; not applied; DuplicateKeyConflict case open
Individually above a value or risk threshold, a near-duplicate, or awaiting per-record affirmation
An authorized person excluded it, with reason
Command receipted; carries the command id
Command completed successfully
Command refused by business rules at execution, exactly as for an interactive request
External effect ambiguous; reconciliation obligation open (CNV-PAY-004)

transitions.authorization: profile rules and handler validate mode
conflict case decision: the correcting record is processed through a compensating command or observation
run submission (guards as for Run Submitting)

proposed_state_mapping.reason: An expectation exists before any file; it is its own entity
Needed for interrupted-upload and orphan reconciliation
Receipt and quarantine are the same commit; a received-but-not-quarantined state would be a window where unsafe bytes are addressable
Owner requirement (unbound#18)
Queue position is operational detail of the inspection command, already tracked by Echelon.Execution
As above; a lease, not a business state
Terminal security outcome
Structure and business validation run in one isolated pass; splitting them adds a state without adding a decision
No decision happens between structure and business validation

proposed_state_mapping.maps_to: record outcome Invalid, or Run.Held when a threshold is breached, or Run.Rejected for structural failure
proposed_state_mapping.reason: Failure is usually per record; whole-run failure is a threshold or structural decision
Only when the business commands themselves require approval; files never require approval merely for being files
A state with no possible decision; approval satisfied means submit
Distinguishes 'commands being created' from 'commands executing'

proposed_state_mapping.maps_to: Run.Completed (or CompletedWithUnknowns) with per-record outcome counts
proposed_state_mapping.reason: Partial is a property of outcomes, not a phase
Completed means every record outcome is final
Reconciliation scope is an account-date, not a file; one file may feed several scopes and one scope several files
As above

proposed_state_mapping.maps_to: exception case (work item) referencing any entity; Run.Held where a person must decide before processing continues
proposed_state_mapping.reason: An exception is a work item about a state, not a state; modelling it as a state loses which state it interrupted
Pre-submission correction; post-submission correction is by reversal
Archive tier is a cost optimisation, not a business state
Terminal with tombstone
